title: Opposite transports in a bicartesian interval fibration are adjoint
statement:
Use the canonical composition classes of [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition]. Use quasicategories, coherent functors, transformations, mapping spaces and homotopies from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and cartesian and cocartesian fibrations from [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. Let $p:E\to\Delta^1$ be both a cartesian and a cocartesian fibration, with fibers $E_0,E_1$. Suppose $R:E_1\to E_0$ is equipped with a coherent map $h:\Delta^1\times E_1\to E$ over $\Delta^1$, whose endpoints are $R$ and the inclusion of $E_1$, and whose edge at every object of $E_1$ is $p$-cartesian. Then there exist a functor $L:E_0\to E_1$ and a coherent map $k:\Delta^1\times E_0\to E$ over $\Delta^1$, with endpoints the inclusion of $E_0$ and $L$, whose edges at objects are $p$-cocartesian. These transport functors have a coherent adjunction $L\dashv R$. Explicitly, there are coherent transformations $\eta:\mathrm{id}_{E_0}\to RL$ and $\epsilon:LR\to\mathrm{id}_{E_1}$, with homotopies $R\epsilon\circ\eta R\simeq1_R$ and $\epsilon L\circ L\eta\simeq1_L$ in the corresponding coherent functor categories. The adjunct maps
$$\operatorname{Map}_{E_1}(Ly,z)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Map}_{E_0}(y,Rz),\qquad v\longmapsto R(v)\circ\eta_y$$
are equivalences, coherently natural in $y,z$. This conclusion includes the higher compatibility of the transformations and homotopies, rather than only triangle equations in the ordinary homotopy categories of $E_0,E_1$.

source.place: Proposition 6.2.5.4 (02FN), the bicartesian-to-adjunction direction; Remark 6.2.5.3 (02FM), existence and description of transport functors; Definitions 5.2.2.4 (019N) and 5.2.2.15 (01VN), the transport witnesses; Proposition 6.2.1.17 (02F1), the induced adjunct equivalence. Coherent adjunction has the unit/counit and triangle meaning of Definition 6.2.1.1 (02EK). Read online 2026-10-17; not archived. Kerodon identifiers, not Stacks tags.
